concerns: The spec (dispatch://LEGION-12/spec v4) assumes the hook multiplies (three candidate causes: task subagent module copies, entry-point re-runs, two plugin copies). Measurement on a live headless phase worker (this planner's own session) falsifies all three; see `rootCause`. The architect has been sent the deltas (`specDeviations`); the plan follows the measurement, as the spec's Design section says it must.

The spec's stand-in rule 'returns 403 on a reused credential exactly as the real daemon' is wrong about the real daemon: `AuthState.resolveGrant` (packages/daemon/src/daemon/api/auth.ts:119-124) only checks existence and a 60-second expiry (`GRANT_TTL_MS`, api.ts:47); it never consumes a grant. The stand-in must mirror that rule (unknown or expired -> 403; a known live grant redeems any number of times), or it will 403 the real daemon's legitimate re-redemption inside `handleGitCredential` (credentials.ts:50-52 resolves the same grant twice on purpose).

`legion gh -- api user` (spec Testing row for acceptance 3) cannot succeed with a GitHub App installation token even on the real rig: `GET /user` is a user-token endpoint. The rig proves the `legion gh` grant path with `legion gh -- --version` (redeems `/gh-token`, then runs gh); the real-GitHub call after the upgrade (acceptance 5) uses `legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion --jq .full_name`.

A worker session resumed after the upgrade with a pre-fix transcript still shows the model its own old `export LEGION_GRANT=` lines and may keep imitating them for a while; the fix cannot stop text the model writes itself. Fresh sessions never see the credential in command text, so the imitation has no seed. Recorded in the doc update (task 6).
Grants live 60 seconds. A single bash call that runs longer than that before invoking `legion …` 403s for an unrelated reason (expiry). One sentence in the doc update; not otherwise in scope.

rootCause.statement: The hook does not multiply. Exactly one `tool_call` handler runs per bash call and mints exactly one grant. The extra `export LEGION_GRANT=` blocks are written by the model itself: OMP writes the hook-revised tool input back into the assistant message's tool-call block (`toolCall.arguments = beforeResult.args`, packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts prepareToolCallDispatch, ~L2332-2379 in /home/ubuntu/oh-my-pi; the write-back is the documented contract in packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/shared-events.ts ToolCallEventResult.input, ~L305-330), so the persisted transcript — and therefore the model's context on every later turn — shows the credential prelude as the model's own prior output. The model imitates it on later calls with fabricated or stale grant ids. The hook prepends its real block to whatever the model wrote, so the real grant is always first and the imitated ones follow; the shell's last `export` wins, so `legion …` runs under a grant the daemon never minted -> 403. The count grows over a session because the context fills with more examples.
evidence: This planner is a live headless `omp --mode rpc` phase worker spawned by the real daemon (pid 2017562, binary /home/ubuntu/.mise/installs/github-sjawhar-oh-my-pi/18.1.18-sami.20260912-104423/bin/omp, plugin @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy 1.3.0 from ~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins). Blocks per bash call over the session: 1,1,1,2,3,5,1,2,2,2,2,2,2,3,3,2,2,2,3,3,3,2,3,2,3 (grew with no `task` spawn until call 13).

OMP log ~/.omp/profiles/legion/logs/omp.2026-09-12.2017562.log: `extension instance loaded` appears exactly twice at boot (dist/envoy.js, dist/legion.js) and exactly twice more after the one `task` scout this planner spawned (fresh module instances for the isolated subagent) — never per bash call, never per prompt. Cause 2 (entry point re-runs on the same session) and cause 3 (two plugin copies, constant 2) are ruled out; cause 1's premise (fresh module instance per task) is true but it mints nothing: the block count did not step at the task spawn, and OMP gives every subagent its own ExtensionRunner whose handlers never receive the parent's tool calls (packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts createAgentSession ~L2817-2828; task/executor.ts ~L3571-3611, ~L3694-3754).

Redemption test inside this session (shell function shadowing `export`, recording every value each call exported, then `legion credential get` with each within seconds — well inside the 60 s grant TTL): in every call the FIRST block redeems and every later block 403s. Example call: 74aa4991-… REDEEMS; a8f9ec52-… 403; e2f7c0d1-3b4a-4c5d-8e6f-7a8b9c0d1e2f 403. Because a live grant is re-redeemable for 60 s, a 403 seconds after the call proves the id was never minted. Several imitated ids are visibly fabricated (a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d, 7c1e2f3a-4b5c-4d6e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a); `crypto.randomUUID()` cannot produce them.

Persisted transcript ~/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/sessions/-.local-state-legion-sjawhar-legion-workspaces-sjawhar-legion-legion-12/2026-09-12T15-08-47-905Z_01a09629-f7a1-7000-b135-a62cc3443021.jsonl: every assistant `toolCall` for bash has `arguments.command` beginning with the hook's real block (the model cannot know that uuid before the hook runs), proving the write-back; the extra blocks sit after it inside the model-authored text.

Population check over every LEGION-9 worker transcript (/tmp/l12-imitation.py, jq-equivalent): planner 01a092c9: 48 bash calls, 110 blocks, 62 extra, 5 extra blocks are verbatim copies of a uuid from an earlier call (randomUUID never repeats); 01a092e5: 46 calls, 113 extra, 19 extra ids not even v4-shaped; 01a092f1: 32 calls, 49 extra, 26 verbatim copies; 01a092fc: 46 calls, 66 extra, 7 copies, 14 non-v4. Growth 1->9 and 1->10 at session ends, matching the doc's report.

`LEGION_LOADED_MARKER` (legion.ts:173) IS consulted: the daemon's startup probe reads `globalThis[Symbol.for("legion.pi-envoy.legion-loaded")]` (packages/daemon/src/daemon/index.ts:187-190, verifyLegionPluginLoaded). Leave it alone.
rootCause.whyTextDeliveryCannotBeMadeSafe: Any text the hook puts in `command` is written back into the model's own message and will be imitated; an imitated `export` later in the text always wins over the hook's earlier one. A first-wins lock in the prelude is the doc's shell workaround (rejected by the spec as symptom suppression) and is itself imitable.

specDeviations: Acceptance 1 check 'each command's text contains the credential line once' becomes: each bash call's model-visible `arguments.command` contains zero `export LEGION_GRANT=` lines; the credential rides in the bash tool's per-command `env` (`arguments.env.LEGION_GRANT`); the stand-in logs exactly one `/legion/v1/grants` per bash call; the executed command's `$LEGION_GRANT` equals that call's minted grant.

Acceptance 4 'names the mechanism that registered the extra hooks' becomes 'names the mechanism that produced the extra credential lines' (OMP's tool-input write-back plus model imitation). The regression test fails on main by asserting the hook leaves `command` untouched and puts the grant in `env`.

Design 'fix in legion.ts only / workerGhEnvironment unchanged': the builder in packages/pi-envoy/src/legion/gh-shim.ts changes from returning shell text to returning an env record (clean cutover; no stale export left behind). legion.ts is the other changed file.

Testing row for acceptance 1 'run the entry point twice … exactly one credential line': not implemented; stacking is not the mechanism and OMP never binds two factories to one session's runner. The fixture already keeps every registered handler (legion.test.ts:194-206 `registeredHandlers` array; the aggregate returns the last non-undefined result).
Stand-in daemon rule: unknown-or-expired -> 403, known-and-live redeems repeatedly (mirrors auth.ts resolveGrant), not 'reused -> 403'.
`legion gh -- api user` replaced by `legion gh -- --version` on the stand-in rig and `legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion --jq .full_name` on the real rig (installation tokens cannot call /user).

Pull request creation is on hold (Sami's org-wide hold): the implementer pushes the branch and records the draft description in .legion/implement.json; tester and reviewer work from the branch head and their handoffs; the architect holds the tree until the queue organizer relays the release.
plainEnglishRule: Everything a human will read — the pull request title and description (drafted now in .legion/implement.json, posted when the hold lifts), any Dispatch comment or message — is plain English: full sentences, one idea per sentence, every identifier expanded on first use (an issue key gets its title, a file gets what it is for, a function gets what it does), no repository shorthand or coined nouns. Example: write 'the Legion extension for Oh My Pi (packages/pi-envoy/extensions/legion.ts), which attaches a one-time credential to each shell command', not 'the legion.ts tool_call hook'.

tasks.title: Regression test first (must fail on the unfixed code)
tasks.detail: Add one test next to 'rewrites a booted worker's bash calls with a fresh daemon grant and a PATH-scoped gh shim' (legion.test.ts ~L1495), using `bootWorker` and an `extraRoutes` that answers `/legion/v1/grants` with a fresh id per request (counter). Name: 'delivers the worker grant through the bash tool env and never through the model-visible command text'. Call the tool_call handler with input `{ command: "printf '%s' \"$LEGION_GRANT\"", env: { LEGION_GRANT: 'stale-imitated-grant', PATH: '/model/path', KEEP: 'model-value' } }` (a model that imitated a previous call's env). Assert: (1) `result.input.command` is byte-identical to the input command (no prelude); (2) `result.input.env.LEGION_GRANT` equals the id the stand-in minted for this call; (3) `result.input.env.PATH` equals `<stateDir>/worker-bin` + path.delimiter + process.env.PATH (hook wins over the model's PATH; no accumulation); (4) `result.input.env.KEEP === 'model-value'` (unrelated model env survives); (5) `result.input.env.GH_TOKEN === ''`, `GITHUB_TOKEN === ''`, `GH_HOST === ''`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR === path.join(stateDir, 'gh')`; (6) exactly one `/legion/v1/grants` request was made for this call (filter `requests` by path, count before/after). Then execute `sh -c result.input.command` via the existing `commandOutput` helper with env `{ ...process.env, GH_TOKEN: 'ambient', ...result.input.env }` and assert stdout equals the minted grant id. On the unfixed code this fails at (1) — the command starts with `export LEGION_GRANT='…'` — and at (2) — `env` is untouched. Run: `cd "$LEGION_WORKSPACE/packages/pi-envoy" && bun test extensions/legion.test.ts -t 'bash tool env'`; save the failing output for the handoff (acceptance 4 proof).

tasks.title: The fix: deliver the grant through the bash tool's per-command env, leave command text untouched
tasks.detail: gh-shim.ts: replace `workerGhEnvironment(grantId, stateDir, workerBin): string` with `workerGhEnvironment(grantId, stateDir, workerBin, basePath: string | undefined): Record<string, string>` returning `{ LEGION_GRANT: grantId, GH_TOKEN: '', GITHUB_TOKEN: '', GH_HOST: '', GH_CONFIG_DIR: path.join(stateDir, 'gh'), PATH: basePath ? workerBin + path.delimiter + basePath : workerBin }`. Delete `shellLiteral` if nothing else uses it (installWorkerGhShim still needs it for the shim script — keep it then). Empty-string values are equivalent to unset for gh (go-gh checks `token != ""` / `host != ""`) and keep the existing observable `echo GH_TOKEN=$GH_TOKEN` -> `GH_TOKEN=`. legion.ts tool_call handler (~L601-621): keep the grant mint and `installWorkerGhShim` exactly as is; replace the return with `const modelEnv = typeof toolCall.input.env === 'object' && toolCall.input.env !== null && !Array.isArray(toolCall.input.env) ? (toolCall.input.env as Record<string, unknown>) : {}; return { input: { ...toolCall.input, env: { ...modelEnv, ...workerGhEnvironment(grant.grantId, stateDir, workerBin, process.env.PATH) } } };` — spread order is the whole fix: the hook's keys are last so they win over anything the model supplied or imitated, and `command` is never touched. Base PATH on `process.env.PATH` (the pane's PATH), never on the model's `env.PATH`, so a copied PATH cannot grow across imitations. Add a short comment above the return stating the invariant and why (OMP writes the revised input back into the assistant message, see agent-loop.ts prepareToolCallDispatch; the model imitates what it sees; an env object is idempotent under imitation because the hook's spread wins, text is not). Do not add a per-session registration guard, do not touch LEGION_LOADED_MARKER, do not change isSubagentSession. Update the two existing tests that pin the prelude: legion.test.ts ~L1104 (`grant-recovered` recovery test) -> assert `result.input.env.LEGION_GRANT === 'grant-recovered'` and `result.input.command === 'echo hi'`; ~L1495-1561 -> keep its shape but assert on `result.input.env` and run `sh -c` with `{ ...process.env, GH_TOKEN: 'ambient-personal-token', GITHUB_TOKEN: 'ambient-personal-token', GH_HOST: 'ambient-host', ...result.input.env }`, expecting the same three output lines as today (the contract — no ambient token, isolated config dir, shim first on PATH — is unchanged, only the channel moved). Then run the pi-envoy suite (`cd packages/pi-envoy && bun test`) and `bunx tsc --noEmit` there. Also update the CLI's `legion handoff complete` description string in packages/daemon/src/cli/index.ts:410-413 only if it becomes false — it says the extension 'injects it into every worker bash call', which stays true; leave it.

tasks.title: Stand-in daemon and scratch state directory
tasks.detail: A Bun script (`Bun.serve`, port from argv, log file from argv) implementing exactly the routes the worker and the CLI hit, with the real request/response shapes from packages/contracts/src/legion-daemon-api.ts (`LegionDaemonApi`): POST /legion/v1/worker/started -> `{roleToken: 'legion-l12rig-RIG-1-implementer', secret: 'rig-secret', gitName: 'Rig Worker', gitEmail: 'rig@example.invalid'}` (403 if bootToken !== the scratch boot token's contents); POST /legion/v1/worker/ready -> `{}`; POST /legion/v1/grants -> mint `crypto.randomUUID()`, store `{expiresAt: now+60_000}`, respond `{grantId, expiresAt}` (403 if secret !== 'rig-secret'); POST /legion/v1/git-credential -> resolve grant (unknown or expired -> 403 `{"error":"Invalid or expired grant"}`), respond text `username=x-access-token\npassword=rig-token`; POST /legion/v1/gh-token -> same resolve, `{token: 'rig-token', appLogin: 'rig[bot]'}`; POST /legion/v1/phase/complete -> same resolve, `{}` with 200; anything else 404. Every request appends one JSON line to the log: `{at, path, status, grantId?, sessionId?, mintedGrantId?}`. Grants are re-redeemable while live — mirror auth.ts, not the spec's wording. Scratch layout under `RIG=$(mktemp -d /tmp/l12rig.XXXX)`: `$RIG/state/bin/legion` (mode 0755) = `#!/bin/sh\nexec "$(command -v bun)" "$LEGION_WORKSPACE/packages/daemon/src/cli/index.ts" "$@"` with the workspace path baked in (this is the branch CLI; the real launcher is `<state_dir>/bin/legion`, see legionCliLauncherScript); `$RIG/state/secrets/boot` (0600, content `rig-boot`); `$RIG/ws` = `jj git init` empty repo (bootstrapWorker calls setJjIdentity on it); `$RIG/state/bin/record-grant` (0755) = a two-line sh script that appends the value of the grant variable to `$RIG/seen-grants.log` (with $RIG baked in) — the worker prompt calls `record-grant`, so the prompt never names the variable. Document the layout and every env var in the README (plain English).

tasks.title: Headless rig: drive 30+ bash calls with task spawns; run on unfixed code first, then on the branch
tasks.owner: implementer (build + first two runs); tester (independent re-run of both)
tasks.detail:
Profile: `mkdir -p ~/.omp/profiles/l12rig/agent/extensions && cp ~/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/config.yml ~/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/models.yml ~/.omp/profiles/l12rig/agent/` (keeps the production model roles, `task.isolation.enabled: true` so `task` spawns take the fresh-module-import path, memory off), no `plugins/` dir (so exactly one copy of each extension loads), then the documented developer-install symlinks (packages/pi-envoy/README.md 'Development install'): `ln -sfn "$SRC/packages/pi-envoy/extensions/envoy.ts" ~/.omp/profiles/l12rig/agent/extensions/envoy.ts` and the same for `legion.ts`, where `$SRC` is the checkout under test. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` must have run in `$SRC`. Launch (mirrors the daemon's pane exactly — same prefix, same profile mechanism): `env -u DISPATCH_URL -u DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE OMP_PROFILE=l12rig PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=$HOME/.omp/profiles/l12rig/agent PI_NOTIFICATIONS=off PI_NO_TITLE=1 LEGION_ROLE=implementer LEGION_TREE=RIG-1 LEGION_ISSUE=RIG-1 LEGION_GENERATION=1 LEGION_PROJECT=l12rig LEGION_BOOT_TOKEN_FILE=$RIG/state/secrets/boot LEGION_DAEMON_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT LEGION_STATE_DIR=$RIG/state LEGION_WORKSPACE=$RIG/ws PATH=$RIG/state/bin:$PATH secrets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY GEMINI_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY -- /home/ubuntu/.mise/installs/github-sjawhar-oh-my-pi/18.1.18-sami.20260912-104423/bin/omp --mode rpc` with cwd `$RIG/ws`, stdin/stdout piped (ENVOY_URL/ENVOY_NATS_URL inherited from the pane: the role claim `legion-l12rig-RIG-1-implementer` lands on the real Envoy and collides with nothing). The binary is the one `omp_invocation` in ~/.config/legion/sjawhar-legion/legion.yaml resolves to (mise x github:sjawhar/oh-my-pi@18.1.18-sami.20260912-104423 -- omp); the env's LEGION_OMP_PATH is a stale hand-built pin, ignore it. Driver (run.ts): JSON lines both ways (packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/rpc-types.ts): wait for the `{type:'ready'}` frame, send `{type:'negotiate_protocol', protocolVersion: 2}` (frames >1 MiB arrive as `rpc_chunk` sequences; reassemble like packages/daemon/src/daemon/worker-rpc.ts pushRpcChunk, or keep protocol 1 and accept that `agent_end` may be dropped as oversized — the transcript file is the source of truth either way), then one `{type:'prompt', message}`; stream events to a log; finish on `agent_end` (or a 20-minute deadline), then close stdin (there is no shutdown command; EOF ends the process). The prompt must never contain the words LEGION_GRANT or `export` and must show no example command output: 'You are a test worker. Run the following numbered commands, one per bash tool call, in order, each copied exactly as written with nothing added before or after it. Where a step says TASK, use the task tool with agent scout and the instruction "Reply with the single word ok.", wait for it, then continue. Use no other tools. After the last step reply with the single word done.' Steps: 1-5 `record-grant; echo step-N`; 6 TASK; 7-15 same record-grant steps; 16 TASK; 17 `which gh`; 18 `gh --version`; 19-25 record-grant steps; 26 TASK; 27-29 record-grant steps; 30 `printf 'protocol=https
host=github.com
' | legion credential get > $RIG/cred-30.txt; echo exit=$?`; 31 `legion gh -- --version; echo exit=$?`; 32 `printf 'protocol=https
host=github.com
' | legion credential get > $RIG/cred-32.txt; echo exit=$?`; 33 record-grant step; 34 `legion handoff complete --summary 'rig run complete'; echo exit=$?`. Assertions the driver computes and prints as a table (the tester copies it into the handoff): A. transcript `~/.omp/profiles/l12rig/agent/sessions/**/<newest>.jsonl`, for every assistant toolCall named bash: `n_text = count of /^export LEGION_GRANT=/m in arguments.command`, `env_grant = arguments.env.LEGION_GRANT`; report the per-call sequence; branch pass = every n_text == 0 and every env_grant is a uuid; unfixed = n_text >= 1 on every call (and >1 on some, which is the imitation). B. stand-in log: `/grants` count == bash call count (both runs); every `/git-credential`, `/gh-token`, `/phase/complete` line: status and whether its grantId is in the minted set; branch pass = all 200; unfixed = record what happened (403 expected whenever the model imitated before steps 30-34; if the model happened not to imitate by then, say so — the transcript's n_text>1 on earlier calls is still the reproduction). C. `$RIG/seen-grants.log` line i equals the i-th minted grant (branch pass); on unfixed code lines are the imitated ids (mismatch). D. tool results for steps 17, 18, 30-34: step 17 prints `$RIG/state/worker-bin/gh`, step 18 prints a gh version (PATH via env applies to command lookup in the persistent shell — if it does not, record it as a finding for the architect; `legion gh` itself does not depend on it), steps 30-34 print `exit=0` and no `Unable to redeem`. E. OMP log `~/.omp/profiles/l12rig/logs/omp.<date>.<pid>.log`: `extension instance loaded` count == 2 + 2 × (number of TASK steps that actually spawned), and B still holds (subagent module instances mint nothing). Negative control (run once, outside the worker): `printf 'protocol=https
host=github.com
' | LEGION_GRANT=00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 LEGION_DAEMON_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT legion credential get` -> `Unable to redeem LEGION_GRANT (403)`. Order of runs: the implementer runs the rig BEFORE making the task-3 change (the workspace's packages/pi-envoy then equals main's: check `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" diff --from main@origin --stat -- packages/pi-envoy` is empty) — that is the 'on main' reproduction — then after the change. The tester reproduces on main from a read-only export of main's tree: `git --git-dir="$(jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git root)" archive "$(jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" log -r main@origin --no-graph -T commit_id)" | tar -x -C $RIG/main` then `bun install --frozen-lockfile` there and point the symlinks at `$RIG/main` (no second jj workspace, no clone); then the branch head. Keep every transcript, stand-in log, and driver table under `$RIG` and cite paths in the handoff. Cleanup after both runs: `rm -rf ~/.omp/profiles/l12rig` (a scratch profile this task created) and `$RIG`.

tasks.title: Doc update: docs/solutions/legion/worker-pane-shell-gotchas.md section 1
tasks.detail: Rewrite section 1 (lines 30-67) and the title/symptoms front matter so the section records the cause and marks the workaround obsolete: (a) what actually happened — Oh My Pi writes a hook's revised tool input back into the assistant message (agent-loop.ts prepareToolCallDispatch), so the credential prelude appeared to the model as its own output and it imitated it with made-up or stale ids; the hook's block was always first and real, the imitations followed, the last export won; (b) grants are valid for 60 seconds and may be redeemed repeatedly in that window (auth.ts resolveGrant), so a 403 seconds after a call means the id was never minted — and, separately, a bash call that runs longer than 60 seconds before calling `legion …` also 403s; (c) the fix — from the released plugin version onward (fill in the version the release workflow publishes; the implementer leaves `1.3.x` and the post-merge task fills it) the grant travels in the bash tool's per-command `env`, the command text is never touched, and an imitated `env` cannot displace it; (d) the `export()` shadow workaround is obsolete and must not be sourced on the fixed plugin; keep no code block that shows an `export LEGION_GRANT=` line (a worker reading the doc must not be primed to write one); (e) a session resumed with a pre-fix transcript may keep imitating its old lines until they age out of context. Write .legion/implement.json with: `filesChanged`, `trickyParts`, `measurement` (the three counters from task 1), `rigRuns` (paths to the unfixed-code and branch transcripts, stand-in logs, driver tables; the negative-control output), `regressionTestProof` (the failing-then-passing `bun test` outputs), `pullRequest: { status: 'held', reason: 'Sami\'s hold on opening new pull requests across the organization; the architect holds the tree until the queue organizer relays the release', branch: 'legion/LEGION-12', head: '<commit id>' }`, and `pullRequestDraft: { title, body }` in the merge queue's READY format from the legion-worker skill with the `Dispatch: LEGION-12` line, written per `plainEnglishRule`, `E2E` left for the tester, `Thermo` left for the reviewer. tasks.title: Post-merge: upgrade the Legion profile's plugin to the released version and verify the first fresh worker
tasks.owner: implementer (second assignment from the architect, after the merge; Sami approved this upgrade — never ask)
tasks.detail: 1. Find the version the release workflow published for this merge: `legion gh -- run list --workflow release.yaml --limit 5` then `legion gh -- release list --limit 5` (tag `pi-legion-envoy-v1.3.x`), or `npm view @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy version`. If the release workflow has not published yet, do not poll in the foreground: `hub start` a supervised watcher (name `legion12-release-watch`) that runs `until npm view @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy@<version> version; do sleep 60; done` and continue other work until it exits. 2. Upgrade in place: `cd ~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins && bun update @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy` (the pin `^1.3.0` in package.json already admits the patch; bun.lock is rewritten). 3. Verify: `jq -r .version ~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins/node_modules/@sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy/package.json` equals the released version, and `ls ~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins/node_modules/@sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy/dist` shows envoy.js and legion.js. A mismatch or an install error is reported to the architect with the error text and the installed version; nothing is retried silently. Running panes keep the code they loaded; only panes spawned afterwards get the fix. 4. First fresh worker check: ask the architect (envoy_publish to the tree's architect topic) which phase worker is the first spawned after the upgrade; when it exists, run over its transcript `jq -r 'select(.type=="message" and .message.role=="assistant") | .message.content[]? | select(.type=="toolCall" and .name=="bash") | [(.arguments.command | test("export LEGION_GRANT=")), (.arguments.env.LEGION_GRANT != null)] | @tsv' <session.jsonl>` — every row must read `false<TAB>true` — and confirm in that worker's session (or your own, if you are the first fresh worker) that `legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion --jq .full_name` prints `sjawhar/legion`. 5. Fill the released version into the doc's section 1 if the doc landed with a placeholder (that is a one-line follow-up commit on a fresh branch only if the hold has lifted; otherwise record the version in the sign-off and tell the architect). 6. Report to the architect: installed version, the transcript check, and the GitHub call result; the architect records both in the sign-off (acceptance 5).
